info.title: Iminify API
info.summary: Compress, convert and resize images, and scan web pages for every image they load.
info.description: Everything the Iminify website does with images, over HTTP. Every request carries a personal access token from Settings > API Tokens as a Bearer token, for an account whose email is verified. Compressions and page scans run in the background: create one, then poll it until it has finished. The guides are at https://www.iminify.com/docs.

post.description:
Send the image itself as a multipart `file`, or its address as `url` and Iminify fetches it. The answer comes straight back with the status `queued` and a `Location` header; the compression runs in the background, usually for a few seconds, so poll the image until its status is `completed`, `already-optimized`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Each image counts one against your daily images and your compressions a minute, whether it came through here or through the website.

The file goes through the same checks as an upload on the website: a format Iminify reads (PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP, GIF, HEIC, HEIF, TIFF, TIF), your plan's file size, a name of at most 128 bytes, and at most 64 megapixels, before and after any resize. An address has to be public `http` or `https`: Iminify fetches it from its own servers, refuses private networks on the address and on every redirect, follows up to five redirects, gives up after 30 seconds and stops as soon as the file passes your plan's size. The file is named after the address. Iminify fetches up to 2 addresses for you at a time; one more sent before those finish is refused with `rate_limited`.

schema.description: The image, as a file or as the address to fetch it from, and the settings to compress it with.

url.description: The public address of the image to fetch. Send either this or `file`.

level.description: How hard to compress. `smart` finds the lowest quality that still looks like your upload, `ultra` goes further and softens fine texture a little, `lossless` changes no pixel, `none` only applies the format, the resize and the metadata choice. See [Compression settings](/docs/compression-settings).

anyOf.description: Convert to this format. `auto` encodes the image in every format that can hold it and keeps the smallest. Leave it out to keep the upload's own format; a HEIC or TIFF always comes back in another one, because Iminify doesn't write either. `jpeg` is read as `jpg`.

keep_metadata.description: Keep the EXIF metadata (camera, date, location) in the optimized copy. Off by default, which strips it; the orientation is applied to the pixels first, so a photo never comes back on its side.

width.description: Resize to this width in pixels. Alone, the height follows the aspect ratio. With `height` too, the image is resized to exactly that size, and its proportions change if they differ. Up to 65535.

height.description: Resize to this height in pixels, the same way as `width`. Up to 65535.

scale.description: Resize to this percentage of the original, 1 to 100. Cannot be combined with `width` or `height`.

alt_text.description: Write an alt text and a suggested file name for the image with AI. On by default; send `false` to leave it out. A small copy of the image goes to Anthropic, whose Claude model writes both, and they arrive a few seconds after the image finishes. Each one counts against your daily AI alt texts; once those are used up the image still compresses, without one. See [Alt text and file names](/docs/images#alt-text-and-file-names).

alt_text_language.description: The language to write the alt text in, as one of these tags: `en` (English), `es` (Spanish), `fr` (French), `de` (German), `it` (Italian), `pt` (Portuguese), `nl` (Dutch), `pl` (Polish), `sv` (Swedish), `tr` (Turkish), `ru` (Russian), `uk` (Ukrainian), `ar` (Arabic), `fa` (Persian), `he` (Hebrew), `hi` (Hindi), `id` (Indonesian), `vi` (Vietnamese), `th` (Thai), `ja` (Japanese), `ko` (Korean), `zh-Hans` (Simplified Chinese), `zh-Hant` (Traditional Chinese). The suggested file name follows it when the language is written in the Latin alphabet, and is in English otherwise.

use_suggested_name.description: Rename the optimized copy to the suggested file name as soon as the alt text arrives, unless it already has a new name by then: yours, or an earlier suggestion.

anyOf.description: The page audit: how the page shows its images (oversized files, missing dimensions, lazy loading in the wrong place, missing alt text, the largest contentful paint), measured in a browser for every image the page had, including the ones past your plan's images per scan. `null` until the scan has finished, for a scan that failed, and for one made before the audit existed. Only on a single scan, not in a list.

share_url.description: The page report's public link while it is shared, or `null`. The link answers only while your plan includes Pro.

rendered.description: Whether a browser opened the page. `false` when only its HTML could be read: then the image addresses are known and nothing about how they are shown, so every finding count is 0.

images_found.description: How many image addresses the page had. `images` lists them all unless a page had more than 1000.

largest_paint.description: The page's largest contentful paint (LCP): the biggest thing in the first screen, which is when a visitor sees the page as loaded. `null` when it could not be measured.

kind.description: `image` (a picture or a background), `text`, or `none` when the page painted nothing.

element.description: The element's tag, such as `img`, `h1` or `div`.

url.description: The image's address, when it is one. The image's own entry in `images` says `largest_paint: true`.

findings.description: How many images have each finding.

oversized.description: Images whose file is more than twice as wide and twice as tall as the space they are shown in.

without_dimensions.description: Images shown without width and height attributes (and no CSS aspect ratio), so the page can move as they load.

lazy_above_fold.description: Images in the first screen that are lazy loaded, which delays them.

eager_below_fold.description: Images below the first screen that are not lazy loaded, so they load before they are needed.

missing_alt.description: Images without alt text. An empty `alt=""`, which marks an image as decorative, is not counted.

lcp_not_prioritized.description: 1 when the largest paint is an image without `fetchpriority="high"`, which would have the browser fetch it first.

oversized_bytes.description: About how many bytes the oversized images would shed if each were served at twice the size it is shown, the size a high density screen draws. An estimate from the share of pixels that would go.

bytes.description: The bytes a browser downloaded for the images listed.

formats.description: How many images arrived in each format, the commonest first, as a browser received them: a site can send a browser WebP or AVIF and the scan's own download the original format.

images.description: Every image address the page had, in the page's order.

url.description: The image's address on the page.

format.description: The format a browser received it in (`jpg`, `png`, `webp`, `avif`, `gif`, `svg`, ...), or `null` when it did not load as an image.

bytes.description: The bytes a browser downloaded for it, or `null` when it did not load as an image.

natural_width.description: The file's own width in pixels, or `null` when it is not shown by an `img` element or did not load.

natural_height.description: The file's own height in pixels.

rendered_width.description: The width it is shown at on a desktop screen 1366 pixels wide, the largest where the page shows it more than once. `null` when no `img` element shows it (a CSS background, a hidden image).

rendered_height.description: The height it is shown at.

above_fold.description: Whether it is in the first screen before scrolling, or `null` when that is not known.

largest_paint.description: Whether it is the page's largest contentful paint.

anyOf.description: Whether it has alt text: `present`, `empty` (`alt=""`, or marked as decorative) or `missing`. `null` when no `img` element shows it.

findings.description: What is worth fixing about it, empty when nothing.

wasted_bytes.description: About how many bytes it would shed at twice the size it is shown, when it is oversized; otherwise `null`.

outcome.description: What the scan did with it. `compressed`: it is one of the scan's images (`image_id`). `skipped`: passed over, with `skip_reason`; a `duplicate` names the image it shares its bytes with in `image_id`. `left_out`: never compressed, because the scan stopped at your plan's images per scan or its time budget, or the image has been deleted since.

anyOf.description: Why it was skipped, the same codes as the scan's `skipped` list, or `null`.

image_id.description: The id of its compressed image, or `null`.

format_sizes.description: What the compressed file came to in each format, smallest first, when the scan's format was `auto` and more than one format was tried; otherwise `null`.

suggested_alt.description: An AI alt text for an image the page shows without one, written from its compressed copy, or `null`: the image has alt text, the scan was asked for none, it is still being written (the scan's `alt_texts_in_progress` counts it), the day's AI alt texts were used up, or the model gave no usable answer. See [Alt text and file names](/docs/images#alt-text-and-file-names).

StoreImageRequest.description: The image, as a file or as the address to fetch it from, and the settings to compress it with.

file.description: The image. Send either this or `url`.

url.description: The public address of the image to fetch. Send either this or `file`.

level.description: How hard to compress. `smart` finds the lowest quality that still looks like your upload, `ultra` goes further and softens fine texture a little, `lossless` changes no pixel, `none` only applies the format, the resize and the metadata choice. See [Compression settings](/docs/compression-settings).

anyOf.description: Convert to this format. `auto` encodes the image in every format that can hold it and keeps the smallest. Leave it out to keep the upload's own format; a HEIC or TIFF always comes back in another one, because Iminify doesn't write either. `jpeg` is read as `jpg`.

keep_metadata.description: Keep the EXIF metadata (camera, date, location) in the optimized copy. Off by default, which strips it; the orientation is applied to the pixels first, so a photo never comes back on its side.

width.description: Resize to this width in pixels. Alone, the height follows the aspect ratio. With `height` too, the image is resized to exactly that size, and its proportions change if they differ. Up to 65535.

height.description: Resize to this height in pixels, the same way as `width`. Up to 65535.

scale.description: Resize to this percentage of the original, 1 to 100. Cannot be combined with `width` or `height`.

alt_text.description: Write an alt text and a suggested file name for the image with AI. On by default; send `false` to leave it out. A small copy of the image goes to Anthropic, whose Claude model writes both, and they arrive a few seconds after the image finishes. Each one counts against your daily AI alt texts; once those are used up the image still compresses, without one. See [Alt text and file names](/docs/images#alt-text-and-file-names).

alt_text_language.description: The language to write the alt text in, as one of these tags: `en` (English), `es` (Spanish), `fr` (French), `de` (German), `it` (Italian), `pt` (Portuguese), `nl` (Dutch), `pl` (Polish), `sv` (Swedish), `tr` (Turkish), `ru` (Russian), `uk` (Ukrainian), `ar` (Arabic), `fa` (Persian), `he` (Hebrew), `hi` (Hindi), `id` (Indonesian), `vi` (Vietnamese), `th` (Thai), `ja` (Japanese), `ko` (Korean), `zh-Hans` (Simplified Chinese), `zh-Hant` (Traditional Chinese). The suggested file name follows it when the language is written in the Latin alphabet, and is in English otherwise.

use_suggested_name.description: Rename the optimized copy to the suggested file name as soon as the alt text arrives, unless it already has a new name by then: yours, or an earlier suggestion.
